results.title: Nebius raises GPU list prices up to 21% while H100 spot sits at $0.79 - CTOL Digital Solutions
highlights:
### What changed in the price list

The Nebius pricing documentation dates two changes. The first took effect on 1 October, when on demand prices per GPU hour rose for four chips. Reuters reported on 17 September that Nebius had announced it, its second price rise in three months.

- B300 went from $7.85 to $9.50, up 21.0 percent, the largest rise.
- B200 went from $7.15 to $8.50, up 18.9 percent.
- H200 went from $4.50 to $5.40, up 20.0 percent.
- H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50, up 16.9 percent, the smallest rise of the four.

The RTX PRO 6000 stayed at $1.80, so the rise did not reach every GPU.

The second change came on 8 October. The preemptible tier, which rents interruptible capacity at a discount, stopped using fixed prices. It moved to dynamic spot pricing that can change every 15 minutes.

One rule in the documentation matters most. The highest spot price is always one cent below the current on demand rate, so the new list price is a ceiling. The floor is $0.79 or $0.99 depending on the chip. The posted price rise matters to a spot buyer only when the market pushes against that ceiling.

results.title: Nebius GPU Price Hike: H100 to B300 Cloud Prices Rise | metir Blog
results.author: Metir AI Team
highlights:
On October 1, 2026, the Nebius GPU price hike took effect: the neocloud raised on-demand rates for Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 instances by roughly 17% to 21%. Nebius's own pricing page now lists the new rates with that effective date and notes that prices exclude taxes and may change at any time (Nebius pricing). It is the second increase in a few months, and it runs against the story most people remember from 2024 and 2025, when GPU rental prices mostly fell.

## What changed in the Nebius GPU price hike

Nebius's pricing page lists these on-demand rates per GPU-hour, before and from October 1: H100 $3.85 to $4.50, H200 $4.50 to $5.40, B200 $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 $7.85 to $9.50 (Nebius pricing). Our arithmetic on those figures gives 16.9%, 20.0%, 18.9% and 21.0%, matching press coverage.

### A note on confirmation

Early coverage disagreed about sourcing. Stocktwits said the details came from Nebius's communication to customers, reshared on Reddit and X, with no official public statement in its report. Silicon UK treated the rates as a Nebius announcement. The question is now largely settled by the company's own pricing page, which shows the October 1 rates. The two reports also differ slightly on timing: Stocktwits was published late on September 16, while Silicon UK dated its report September 18 and said Nebius announced the change "on Thursday."

results.title: Nebius Raises On-Demand GPU Prices Up to 21% From October 1: What an H100 Hour Now Costs | ServerCalc
results.author: ServerCalc Editorial
highlights:
From October 1, 2026, Nebius raised its on-demand, pay-as-you-go rates across its four current Nvidia platforms. On its own published price list the per-GPU-hour numbers now read: H100 NVLink at $4.50, up from $3.85 (about 17%); H200 NVLink at $5.40, up from $4.50 (20%); B200 NVLink at $8.50, up from $7.15 (about 19%); and B300 NVLink at $9.50, up from $7.85 (21%). CPU-only servers were caught in the same round — the AMD EPYC Genoa vCPU now lists at $0.015 per CPU-hour, roughly a quarter more than before. Separately, from October 8 the provider moved preemptible capacity for these platforms onto dynamic spot pricing, so the cheap interruptible tier no longer has a fixed rate.

These are list prices for on-demand use. Committed and reserved terms are quoted separately and run well below the hourly rate; the increase lands hardest on buyers who pay by the hour with no commitment.

results.title: Nebius and CoreWeave Lift Nvidia GPU Prices by Up to 21% - Economic Frame
highlights:
Nvidia rental prices are rising even for last-generation H100s. Nebius has posted an October 1, 2026 on-demand card that lifts selected Nvidia GPU-hour rates by 16.9% to 21.0%. CoreWeave said on September 17 that it is still signing compute at higher prices, including short contracts at about $40 million per megawatt of annualized revenue. A landlord can charge more for a chip it does not make only while that chip stays scarce. That is the signal behind Nvidia, and it is the opposite of a capacity glut.

Nebius’s price page, checked on October 2, still prints two columns. On-demand H100 is $3.85 per GPU-hour. The column marked effective October 1 is $4.50. The same split runs through the H200, the B200, and the B300. Reuters reported on September 17 that this was the second pay-as-you-go increase in about three months, with selected Nvidia GPU rates up 17% to 21%. The card on nebius.com/prices matches that range. It does not show every customer already paying the new rate.

## The card Nebius posted

Four Nvidia rows have a public before and after. GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 racks are still “contact us” in both columns. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. L40S “from” rates do not move. The hike lands on the accelerators customers are queued for.

October 2 is after the effective date, and the page still shows both numbers. The left-hand label is still “On-demand, GPU-hour.” The right-hand label is “GPU-hour (Effective October 1, 2026).” A customer cannot tell, from the page alone, which figure the console will bill.

GPU Finder’s Nebius page, with availability checked at 06:23 UTC on October 2, still listed one-GPU on-demand rates of $3.85 for the H100, $7.15 for the B200, and $7.85 for the B300. Those are the old column. The same check already showed the H200 at $5.40, the new column, with a spot print of $2.45 beside it. The H100 spot print on that row was $2.15. The tracker has not frozen. It has moved one of the four headline GPUs and left the other three on the pre-October number. Treating the whole book as repriced at midnight on October 1 would be tidier, and it would be wrong.

results.title: Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in dollars per GPU-hour:

H100: $3.85 to $4.50
H200: $4.50 to $5.40
B200: $7.15 to $8.50
B300: $7.85 to $9.50

That changed the lowest observed H100 list price across the nine providers we track. On September 27 it was Nebius at $3.85 per GPU-hour. On October 4 it was Crusoe at $3.90.
Everything else held. Of 14,001 GPU price listings in the October 4 catalog, 13,996 matched a September 27 listing, and the 20 Nebius listings were the only verified changes above 1%.

The transaction side moved on its own path. OCPI for H200 went from $4.84 on September 28 to $5.57 on October 4. Over the same stretch, the lowest H200 list price we track held at $4.29 (Crusoe). List prices and transaction prices measure different things, and this week the gap between them widened. If you buy on-demand capacity from a Neocloud, posted price notices are worth tracking. This one landed on schedule, to the cent.

...

These are public catalog list prices, not live quotes, and a listing does not establish capacity or orderability.

Nebius raised H100 prices 17% and H200 prices 20% on September 17, effective October 1. H100 and H200 are two of the GPUs most teams rent for LLM training and inference. If you had an instance running under the old contract, the new rate applies to it now, not at renewal.

You did not choose that new rate. A fixed-term contract works like this: the provider sets a new price, and every running instance inherits it on the provider's schedule. Per-minute billing works differently. You pay whatever rate is posted right now, for the minutes you actually use, and nothing carries forward past that.

results.title: Nebius Publishes Live GPU Spot Prices in European AI Push | TheEnergyMag
results.author: Wolfie Zhao
highlights:
Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) Group NV has made live prices for its interruptible GPU computing capacity publicly available, expanding visibility into cloud costs as it seeks more business from European artificial intelligence developers.

The Amsterdam-based company announced the move at Nvidia’s GTC event in Berlin on Wednesday. Prices are available on its website and through Shadeform, Silicon Data and GPU Finder, according to its statement.

Nebius’s published pricing lists starting spot rates of $0.79 per GPU-hour for Nvidia H100 and H200 processors, compared with on-demand rates of $4.50 and $5.40, respectively. B200 and B300 spot capacity starts at $0.99 per GPU-hour, against on-demand rates of $8.50 and $9.50. Those starting prices exclude taxes and can change with demand and available capacity.

The public display extends a pricing system Nebius announced on September 22 and said would take effect on October 8. That system calculates rates by GPU type and region, with updates as frequently as every 15 minutes. Customers previously viewed current prices when configuring computing resources in the company’s cloud console.
